ai_assessment.method: Full direct German-to-Vietnamese comparison of all 1248 canonical passages and both titles. Separate subagent drafting from the original preceded review. A separate-context assessor (same model family, not shown the drafter’s notes or scores) read every pair first and reported about twenty major and about forty minor findings with a pre-revision weighted score of 8.14; the drafter revised the text, re-read the changed passages and the whole target for naturalness, then assigned these final scores bound to the final byte hashes.
ai_assessment.limitations: The same AI system drafted, revised and assessed the work; the separate-context pass is correlated same-model feedback, not independent review or model diversity. No human literary reviewer, native-reader trial or measured reader demand is claimed. Existing Vietnamese translations were not consulted or collated. Scores are subjective and uncalibrated; missed errors may remain. Source clearance is separately recorded and is not granted by this review.

findings.explanation: Franz’s reading of Karl’s letter called the elder brother “em trai”; now “anh trai”, the sibling seniority of the German.
Same sibling error in Franz’s soliloquy (“Đó là anh trai ngươi!”).
The salutation “Unglücklicher Bruder!” was addressed to the elder Karl; now “Người anh bất hạnh”.
“Auskeuchte” (expired) was rendered as sneezing; corrected.
Amalia’s “Bruder meines Karls” made Franz the elder brother; now “Em trai của Karl”.
The insult “Kastraten-Jahrhundert” lost its central word; restored as “thái giám”.
“Even if half an Our Father” was inverted to “unless”; corrected.
Steps “staggering forward” were rendered as stepping back; corrected.
Amalia’s “Mein, mein!” (mine, mine) was rendered as a denial; now “Của em”.
The antisemitic phrase of Spiegelberg is kept as the source’s content (“làm ăn kiểu Do Thái”), not softened; the editor should confirm this choice.
“Block” as the execution block was rendered as a mat; now a chopping block.
Nachtigall (nightingale) was rendered as a skylark; now họa mi.
“Man vermißt ihn” (he is missed) was rendered as remembering him; corrected.
“Geadelt” (ennobled) was rendered as canonised; corrected.
“Hutschnur” is a hat cord, not a watch chain; corrected.
“Weib” as Moor’s cold address to Amalia had been tender; corrected.
The direction of the avenger was reversed; Franz is to go out to meet him. Corrected.
“Poche dem Tyrannen-Verhängniß” (defy the tyrant’s fate) was rendered as knocking; corrected.
Franz’s “em trai” for Karl, the elder brother, corrected to “anh trai”.
The same sibling reversal at Prag, corrected.
“Mein Bruder” for Karl, corrected to “anh trai của con”.
The relative clause whose subject is freedom’s name had been attached to the men; now attached to tự do.
“Ihn und Ihn” (two men) was rendered as one; corrected.
“Versicherte” (secured) was rendered as bribed; corrected.
“Bettelvögten” (beggar-wardens) was rendered as beggars; corrected.
“Fanger” is a bird-catcher, not a gardener; corrected.
“Bräutigam” (groom) was dropped, leaving the reply without an antecedent; restored.
Minor sense and register fixes in Act II, applied after checking the German.
Minor phrasing fixes in Act V, applied after checking the German.

summary: Full assessment of all 1,248 German/Vietnamese passages: the cast list, the preface and the five acts, translated directly from the German Project Gutenberg text. The first blind reviews of four parts scored 8.00, 8.00, 8.18 and 8.38. Their majors (sibling seniority, where Karl is the elder brother; reversed logic and direction; mistranslated images and idioms; referents) were fixed, and each later round of separate-context blind reviews surfaced further majors, which were fixed in turn. The final reviews score the four parts 8.73 (cast list, preface and Act I), 8.93 (Act II), 8.70 (Acts III–IV) and 8.98 (Act V), with no major or critical finding open. The weakest part, Acts III–IV at 8.70, sets the final score, above the unchanged 8.6 threshold. The editorial choice on the antisemitic phrase in unit 458 and the speaker tag ‘Amalia.’ at unit 337, which mirrors the printed source, are disclosed for the editor.

title_review.rationale: The title is rendered as ‘Bọn cướp’ (The Robbers); no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.
